div.b: Nothing is installed in front of the live application

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1173px; margin-left: 19px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Red Teaming never sits between the application and its real users.
It opens a second door and knocks on it, the same way any other API
client would. Routes 4 and 5 add a component, but that component
carries scan traffic only.
AI Gateway and Network Intercept are the products that do sit in the
live path. Keeping the three apart saves a long conversation with a
customer who has heard that one of them needs a maintenance window.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 664px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1153px; margin-left: 717px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Prefer the adapter over a wrapper wherever Kubernetes exists

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1173px; margin-left: 719px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Routes 4 and 5 solve the same problems. The adapter wins because
Palo Alto Networks manages its execution lifecycle, it already has
private network access through the channel, and there is no extra
internet-facing service to host, patch, and take down afterwards.
Either way the code belongs to the customer. Find out on the
discovery call whether a developer is available, because a target
that needs route 4 or 5 is not a configuration task.
